content:
Hi, does any body know about some Python libraries like numpy, panda, data science related stuff, done in Lean?
If possible please share some links to them.
I found NumpySpec, but it seems very limited in what it does(and has a lot of sorry breaking my confidence in using it)

Thank you
#Project announcements > Tables: a dataframe library
Do you think Mathlib has some direct functions (or atleast almost direct), similar to numpy ones, for basic operations on matrices and tensors?
SciLean is probably the closest match. I started with that but ended up building custom matrix operators to do ML.

Anirudh Gupta said:

Do you think Mathlib has some direct functions (or atleast almost direct), similar to numpy ones, for basic operations on matrices and tensors?

That depends, are you looking to prove things or to run these operations with numpy-like performance?
In either case though, Mathlib's matrices don't have numpy's ergonomics, such as slicing & broadcasting.
I also think they're not performant, but there might be some @[csimp] I'm not aware of.
For performance perhaps you could use nested vectors (docs#Vector), though I think you still won't get a contiguous chunk of memory for the entire matrix.

What goal do you have in mind?

I would like to run things, I want to just import a Correct implementation of an operation, and use it. And hopefully from a trusted source like Mathlib, or some library on github, etc.
I dont mind changing it a little bit, to fit it into my use case, but roughly only superficial edits for my usecase, not rewriting the whole implementation basically
If you don't need performance then I think Mathlib will do. What operations do you need?

Well i will say, I do need performance. But maybe not to the optimized scale of numpy.
Operations commonly used like matrix and tensor operations(addition, multiplication, tensor products), normalization related, etc
There's also https://basisresearch.github.io/lean.py/examples/03_numpy_typed.html which is a wrapper around numpy using lean-py.
